rule.description: A named Go type is a god class when it declares at least 22 methods and those methods collectively drive at least 4 distinct render/serialization engine packages (encoding/json, encoding/csv, encoding/xml, text/template, html/template, go.yaml.in/yaml/v3, github.com/gookit/color). One type then owns the formatting responsibilities of several output domains: format dispatch, issue stream filtering, presentation ordering, per-format serialization and template rendering.
rule.definition: flag type T when methods(T) >= 22 and engines(methodBodies(T)) >= 4; report one match per file that declares methods of T, enumerating the method names declared in that file

checks.description: Detect one named type that centralizes the rendering of multiple output domains: at least 22 declared methods whose bodies collectively drive at least 4 distinct render/serialization engine packages.
checks.detected_relation: type Renderer -> absorbed rendering responsibilities of the csv, golint, html, json, yaml and text format packages plus the report dispatch, suppression filtering, colorization and presentation ordering
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A single type owns the whole report pipeline: it dispatches formats, filters suppressed findings, serializes csv/json/yaml/golint, compiles the text and html templates, colorizes severities, reconstructs code snippets, and assembles the junit, sonarqube and sarif payloads. The per-format owners were reduced to forwarding shims, so distinct presentation responsibilities are no longer separated into cohesive owners.

matches.evidence: The god class anchor file: declares the Renderer struct with the shared out/data/format/enableColor/rootPaths state and the three severity color schemes, a builder chain (forFormat, withColor, withRootPaths), and absorbs the whole dispatch (Render) plus the suppression pipeline (applySuppressionPolicy, filterOutSuppressedIssues) that used to live in report/formatter.go; it also hosts the CLI presentation ordering (OrderIssuesForReport, IssueLeadingLine) that used to live in cmd/gosec/sort_issues.go.

Byte-per-format rendering absorbed from the format packages: renderJSON and renderYAML (encoding/json and go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 marshal of the whole report), renderCSV with csvRecord (encoding/csv), renderGolint with golintCweLabel and issuePositionStart (positional golint messages). The emit helper threads every byte-oriented format through one receiver-owned stream write.

Template-driven formats absorbed from the text and html packages: renderText and renderHTML with their pattern builders, the gookit/color severity palettes stored on the renderer (initColorSchemes, highlightFinding, textFuncMap), plus the code-snippet reconstruction family (renderCodeSnippet, issueCodeRange) and the embedded template assets moved into the coordinator package.

Summary-report assembly absorbed at the byte stage: renderJUnit re-implements the junit xml marshal and xml-header emission around junit.GenerateReport, renderSonar re-implements the sonarqube json indentation around sonar.GenerateReport, and renderSARIF wires the sarif writer into the receiver state (out, data, rootPaths).

excluded.reason: report/sarif is a cohesive subsystem with its own schema builder, types and generator; its methods do not approach the excessive-method threshold on the clean state (ToolComponent declares 11 methods) and it was not absorbed wholesale.

junit.GenerateReport, sonar.GenerateReport and their exported types keep their per-format homes; only the byte-assembly stage was centralized, so these packages are not credited as god-class locations.
gosec.Analyzer (20 methods) and taint.Analyzer (21 methods) fall below the excessive-method threshold of the rule and are not flagged on the clean or injected repository.
